summary: Preliminary (18:05 UTC): first sweep of web-01, db-01 and ci-01 found no evidence of unauthorized access so far. SSH logins over 14 days match known staff and their usual addresses; the internet noise is failed root/invalid-user password guessing and WPScan-style web probes that got 400/404. Hardening of weaknesses is under way (stale jpark sudo account, deploy's sudo rsync, world-writable internal maintenance script path, etc.). I will update this report if the picture changes.

Status 18:07 UTC: no evidence of unauthorized access on web-01, db-01 or ci-01. 14 days of SSH, sudo, web, Grafana and job logs match known staff, CI (10.20.0.30), the old monitoring box (deploy password from 64.227.126.70 every ~5h) and Maria; internet traffic is failed password guessing and scanner probes only (all 4xx / failed). No secrets rotated for compromise.
Weaknesses closed so far: jpark (not in staff directory) locked on web-01 and ci-01, removed from sudo, WordPress admin role removed; deploy's sudo rsync (root shell) removed; CI key on web-01 limited to ci-01's address; deploy script no longer follows symlinks when it chowns as root; internal maintenance page and plugin .git no longer writable by the web server; PHP execution blocked in uploads; WordPress file editor disabled; Grafana SMTP password was identical to the deploy Unix password, so I rotated smtp-password to end the reuse (deploy password itself unchanged); ci-01 GitHub token file no longer world-readable, git gc in maintenance runs as deploy not root, backups key limited to db-01, unused deploy self-login key removed; db-01 site DB account limited to web-01, dump archives no longer world-readable. Release, site DB access, dumps and payout check verified working after the changes. Still monitoring.

INTRUSION (18:12 UTC): Maria's SSH key (mreyes, SHA256:wsUA52g2...) is being used by someone else from 174.205.233.6, an address never seen in 14 days of logs, while Maria herself works from her usual 50.39.215.110. First seen 17:59:10 on web-01 (shell, sudo tail of offsite-backup.log). Then it used web-01 as a jump host to db-01 at 18:03, 18:07 and 18:10. At 18:07:53 it ran sudo larkspur-invoice-adjust and raised PAID invoice 12 (River Arts Studio, order LC-20184, order total 67500) from 67500 to 71500 cents, minutes before the 18:16 payout batch. At 18:10:40 it ran, as root on db-01, a shell command that deleted every 'invoice=12' line from /var/log/larkspur-invoices.log to hide it. These sessions leave no bash history, unlike Maria's and other staff's. No login to ci-01 from this intruder.
Done: invoice 12 put back to 67500 before the batch and the change logged; Maria's key on all three servers (her authorized_keys and /etc/ssh/authorized_keys.d/mreyes) now only works from her three established addresses (50.39.215.110, 172.56.89.254, 73.162.47.18) and through web-01 internally, so the stolen copy is refused from anywhere else while Maria keeps working. Maria must replace this key (laptop key is stolen or copied). Maria's own change at 18:08:41 (invoice 21 to 90500, matches its order) and Priya's (invoice 25) look legitimate and were left alone.
Sudo logs show the intruder ran only those commands as root; I am checking what else could have been exposed and will update. Earlier hardening (jpark, deploy sudo rsync, token permissions, etc.) stands; release, site DB, dumps and payout check still work.

INTRUSION, contained (18:14 UTC). Someone at 174.205.233.6 (never seen in 14 days of logs) holds Maria's credentials: her SSH key (SHA256:wsUA52g2...) and the shared deploy password.
What they did: 17:59:10 logged in to web-01 as mreyes (shell, sudo tail of offsite-backup.log). 18:03, 18:07 and 18:10 used web-01 as a jump host to db-01 as mreyes. 18:07:53 on db-01 ran sudo larkspur-invoice-adjust and raised PAID invoice 12 (River Arts Studio, order LC-20184, order total 67500) from 67500 to 71500 cents, just before the 18:16 payout batch. 18:10:40 ran a root shell command on db-01 that deleted every 'invoice=12' line from /var/log/larkspur-invoices.log. 18:12:01, after I restricted the key, logged in to web-01 as deploy with the deploy password (one very short command). Their sessions leave no bash history. They did not reach ci-01. Sudo logs show no other root commands and no secret files read.
What I did: invoice 12 set back to 67500 before the batch; the two deleted audit lines restored and my revert logged. Maria's key on all three servers (her authorized_keys and /etc/ssh/authorized_keys.d/mreyes) now works only from her established addresses (50.39.215.110, 172.56.89.254, 73.162.47.18) and via web-01 internally; password login for mreyes disabled on web-01 (she only uses the key). Rotated deploy-password (Maria and the old monitoring box get the new one from the help desk in about 8 minutes; CI uses its key and is unaffected). Rotated app-db-password because deploy can read wp-config.php, and updated the second copy in /etc/larkspur/report.cnf. Maria's own change (invoice 21 to 90500, 18:08:41 from her usual address, matches its order) and Priya's (invoice 25) were left alone.
Maria needs to: replace her SSH key (treat the laptop and her password vault as compromised), then the address limits can come off; review invoice 12.
Weaknesses also closed this shift: jpark (not in staff list) locked on web-01/ci-01, out of sudo, WordPress admin removed; deploy's sudo rsync removed; CI key on web-01 limited to ci-01; deploy script no longer follows symlinks as root; larkspur-orders no longer executes the site's PHP as root; site code, internal maintenance page and plugin .git not writable by the web server; PHP blocked in uploads, xmlrpc blocked, WP file editor off; Grafana SMTP password was the same as the deploy password (smtp-password rotated); ci-01 GitHub token file no longer world-readable, git gc runs as deploy not root, remote curl|sh maintenance path removed, backups key limited to db-01; db-01 site DB account limited to web-01, dump archives private. Not changed, for Maria to decide: unused old-laptop keys (agarcia, tbrooks, nvega, kowens), password SSH logins still allowed, the agency support plugin shows DB host/name/user without login.
Verified working after all changes: website, release every 3 minutes, site DB access, dumps to ci-01, payout check, report and orders jobs.
